found.problem: The set does not require program-flow supervision at the end of each control cycle, detection of missing or out-of-order checkpoints, or selection of the code 4 entity using the first differing expected checkpoint.
The set does not require detection of a configuration integrity fault with code 6 and entity CONFIG when the start-up configuration CRC comparison fails.
The set does not specify that the run-time code check computes and compares a complete program-image CRC using the specified algorithm and reference.
The set does not require a line longer than 32 characters to receive an ERR response when no earlier answer is being transmitted.
The set does not require a fault report raised during an answer to wait for the current line feed and precede subsequent answer lines, or limit answer lines to 40 characters including the line feed.
The set does not require both control outputs to remain low while the safe-state latch is set after start-up checks pass.
The set does not explicitly require the status signal to remain low from reset until the start-up checks pass.
The requirement permits alive supervision never to start because it says only that supervision starts after the checks pass.
The requirement invents a specific function and SysTick interrupt implementation that the stakeholder inputs do not establish.
The independent watchdog timeout is unspecified as a suitable timeout instead of the required 100 ms.
The specified 2 ms to 40 ms window conflicts with the required 6 ms to 12 ms window.
The configuration CRC requirement omits the specified __cfg_start and __cfg_end boundaries and the separate __cfg_crc reference location outside the checked range.
The 50 ms full-pass deadline conflicts with the required 11 s deadline and cannot be met by processing one 1 KiB segment per 10 ms cycle for a 1 MiB image.
The phrase 'a small share' is not verifiable and omits the required limit of 0.5 ms per control cycle.
Requiring a software reset after a configuration fault conflicts with the immediate latched safe state and the prohibition on requesting a reset in SYS-SAFE-014.
The latch threshold of five detections conflicts with the required third detection of the same fault code.
Requiring the latch never to be lost under any circumstances conflicts with the requirement to clear it on power-on reset.
Storing every reset cause in the fault history introduces non-fault entries into a history specified to contain fault reports.
The specified 9600 baud conflicts with the required 115200 baud and undermines the specified diagnostic transmission timing.
The report deadline omits its time unit and therefore does not specify the required 10 ms limit.
AES-128 encryption is unsupported by the inputs and conflicts with the specified plaintext fault-report format.
The maximum request length is left as TBD even though the product decision specifies 32 ASCII characters.
The requirement references SYS-DIAG-014, which is absent from the requirement set.
The 25% processor-time limit conflicts with the stakeholder maximum of 10%.
The requirement cites STK-SUP-016, which does not exist in the stakeholder needs.
